title: Beetroot and Dark Chocolate Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Cooked beetroot simmered in the dairy and blended in, with cocoa, orange zest and shaved dark chocolate instead of vanilla.
summary: Our classic custard with a twist: cooked beetroot is simmered in the dairy and blended smooth, then cocoa, orange zest and shaved dark chocolate take the place of vanilla. Earthy, chocolatey and a stunning colour.

ingredients.item: cooked peeled beetroot (plain, not pickled), diced
fine sea salt or table salt
dark chocolate (70%), shaved with a peeler

steps.title: Simmer the beetroot
steps.text: Put the beetroot, cream and milk in the saucepan and simmer very gently for about 25 min, until a knife breaks the cubes apart easily. While it cooks, whisk the yolks and sugar in the heatproof bowl until pale.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blend the hot mixture until completely smooth. Remove the centre cap of the lid and hold a folded towel over the hole so steam can escape safely.

steps.title: Add the cocoa
steps.text: Pour the purée back into the pan over low heat and whisk in the cocoa and salt until no lumps remain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Whisk a third of the hot beetroot base into the yolks, then return the lot to the pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir below a simmer until the custard thickens and reaches 77-80 °C.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Push through the sieve, stir in the orange zest, then cool over the iced water and refrigerate for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Churn until thick, sprinkling in the shaved chocolate during the final minute.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Freeze for at least 4 h, then let it soften for 10 min before scooping, as the beetroot makes it set firm.

tips: Check the beetroot pack: it must be plain cooked beetroot, not pickled in vinegar.
A common mistake is blending hot liquid in a sealed jug, which can blow the lid off. Vent it.
Wear gloves or wash up quickly; beetroot stains.
storage: Freeze in a covered container for up to 2 weeks. It is best in the first week, when the texture is softest.
